specialRules.ruleFull:
A Law is not a spell, so protection against spells does not stop it, and it may be used while wearing armour, as a prayer may. A Clockworker who knows Laws rolls for one on a D6:

D6 | Law | Difficulty
1 | Offense | 7
2 | Motion | 6
3 | Defense | 7
4 | Sacrifice | 9
5 | Protection | 7
6 | Rampage | 10

equipmentLists.title: Constructs Equipment List
equipmentLists.caveat: A 1-slot line fills one of the construct's equipment slots and a 2-slot line two; armour goes in its armour slot.

specialRules.ruleFull: Any warrior within 6" of the Master of Clocks may use his Leadership instead of his own.
The Master of Clocks starts with one Law of Construction.
If the Master of Clocks dies or leaves the expedition, the new leader may learn Laws of Construction on later skill advances.
A Dwarf never suffers a movement penalty for wearing armour.
On the Injury chart, treat a roll of 1-2 as knocked down, 3-5 as stunned and 6 as out of action.
A Dwarf ignores the special rules for maces, clubs and the like.
Instead of searching for rare items, the engineer may fit a single construct with any weapon he can get. A two-handed or missile weapon takes two slots, any other weapon one.
Instead of searching for rare items, the Metallurgist may split one moonstone into D6 orichalcum tokens.
Once per game the Metallurgist may throw this tincture as blessed water is thrown, and it sets its target on fire. On a roll of 1 to hit, he is set on fire instead.
When a Handyman rolls That Lad's Got Talent, the new Hero takes Combat and Strength skills as his two skill lists.
At the beginning of your turn roll a D6 for each construct with no friendly Hero within 6", unless it is in close combat. On a 1-2 it may neither move nor shoot this turn.
A construct is immune to psychology and never leaves combat.
A construct treats a stunned result as knocked down.
A construct may not run, but may charge as normal.
A construct is unaffected by poison or drugs.
A construct gains no experience and can only be improved physically.

A weapon or piece of armour given to a construct can never be taken off it again. A construct has equipment slots instead of the usual maximum number of weapons: to give it equipment with no slot free, enough equipment must first be abandoned. A Clockwork soldier has two equipment slots and one armour slot.
Each Clockwork soldier forms a Henchmen group of his own.
At the beginning of your turn roll a D6 for each construct with no friendly Hero within 6", unless it is in close combat. On a 1-2 it may neither move nor shoot this turn.
A construct is immune to psychology and never leaves combat.

A weapon or piece of armour given to a construct can never be taken off it again. A construct has equipment slots instead of the usual maximum number of weapons: to give it equipment with no slot free, enough equipment must first be abandoned. A Clockwork fiend has four equipment slots and one armour slot.
A Clockwork fiend causes fear.
A Clockwork fiend is a Large Target, as the shooting rules define it.
A Moonstone infusion on a Clockwork fiend costs twice as many orichalcum tokens for each characteristic raised.

specialSkillsList.name: Experimental enhancements
specialSkillsList.description: Apprentice only. Instead of searching for rare items, the Apprentice may work on one construct. He needs 3D6 gold crowns of materials, then rolls on the Sealed City's Stygian Mutation chart and applies the result to one of your constructs.

specialSkillsList.name: Moonstone infusion
specialSkillsList.description: Before the game the Hero may raise any characteristic except Toughness and Wounds of a single construct by 1 for each orichalcum token used. Each characteristic may be raised only once, and the increase lasts for that game.

specialSkillsList.name: Puppeteer
specialSkillsList.description: Any construct within 12" of the Hero may ignore the Need Orders rule.

specialSkillsList.name: Rogue control
specialSkillsList.description: Instead of shooting a missile weapon, the Hero may choose a single construct or clockwork weapon within 12" and line of sight. Roll 2D6 against the construct's or the weapon bearer's Leadership: if the roll is higher, the target ceases to function until the Clockworkers' next Movement phase.

specialSkillsList.name: Gift of Sentience
specialSkillsList.description: Instead of searching for rare items, the Hero may spend D3 moonstones on a single Clockwork soldier. The soldier loses Need Orders, Immune to Psychology and Brainless, and re-rolls any That Lad's Got Talent result when rolling for advances.

stubs.name: Orichalcum token
stubs.note: Spent by the Moonstone infusion skill and made by the Metallurgist's Moonstone refinery.

rules.name: Reference work
rules.text: A Clockworker carrying one of these adds 1 to the score when he works out whether a Law of Construction is used successfully.

rules.name: Reload
rules.text: After shooting more than one shot in a single turn the model must spend a whole shooting phase without shooting and out of combat before it may fire again.

rules.name: Salvo
rules.text: The firer may choose to fire three times in the shooting phase. A salvo is at -1 to hit for every shot.

rules.name: Reload
rules.text: After shooting more than one shot in a single turn the model must spend a whole shooting phase without shooting and out of combat before it may fire again.

rules.name: Salvo
rules.text: The firer may choose to fire three times in the shooting phase. A salvo is at -1 to hit for every shot.

stubs.name: Krakensilver Weapon
stubs.note: Four times the price of a normal weapon of its kind, so the price chart prints no figure.

rules.name: Upgrade
rules.text: The buyer chooses which hand-to-hand weapon is offered to him, and it costs four times the price of a normal weapon of that kind. Blunt weapons such as flails and hammers may not be made of krakensilver.
A model attacked by a krakensilver weapon may not parry with a sword, a buckler or the like.

rules.name: Watery stance
rules.text: On solid ground the wielder always loses the roll for who strikes first against an opponent of the same Initiative. Fighting in water he always wins it.

rules.name: Effect
rules.text: The wearer halves any penalty for bad sight conditions, rounding down, and his maximum sight range is 4" longer.

rules.name: Effect
rules.text: A model that lost a limb or an eye to a serious injury or to surgery may have the part replaced. The prosthesis lets him ignore that injury at the cost of one orichalcum token per game; unwilling or unable to pay, he is handicapped by the injury as usual. He does not have to retire if he loses both arms, both eyes or both legs, and may take part in the warband's battles as long as at least one prosthesis is powered; otherwise he misses the battle.

Roll a D6 when the map is bought:

{{table:1}}

rows: The warband finds one more key fragment during its next exploration phase.
The warband may change one dice by -1 or +1 on its next exploration roll.
From now on the warband may always choose to play the city ring's own scenario instead of rolling on the random scenario chart.

stubs.name: Lurking Fear
stubs.note: Not available to Witch Hunters, Warrior-Priests or Sisters of Sigmar.

rules.text: A warrior who takes Lurking Fear before a battle causes fear for that game. It has no effect on Undead such as Vampires and Zombies, or on the Possessed.
Roll 2D6 after the battle. On a 2-3 the warrior is caught in his own aura of fear and from then on permanently treats every enemy model as though it caused fear.
A warrior who takes Moonshine before a battle ignores any penalty for bad sight for that game. It has no effect on Undead such as Vampires and Zombies, or on the Possessed.

Roll a D6 after the battle. On a 1 the warrior's eyesight degrades and he loses 1 Ballistic Skill permanently; if that takes his Ballistic Skill to 0 he is blind and is struck from the warband's roster.

stubs.name: Stardust
stubs.note: Rare 7 for the Maidens of Dusk and Dawn.

rules.text: A model successfully wounded by a weapon coated with stardust must take a Toughness test at once. If it fails it loses 1 Weapon Skill and 1 Ballistic Skill until the end of the battle and always counts as visible, whatever the sight conditions. The loss is permanent.

stubs.name: Gaveleers
stubs.note: Clockwork weapons only; one battle's worth.

rules.text: An enemy wounded by a gaveleer gains +1 on his armour save, and a 6+ armour save if he has none.

rules.name: Smash
rules.text: A model hit by a gaveleer and not wounded by it is knocked down on a 4+.

stubs.name: Shredders
stubs.note: Clockwork weapons only; one battle's worth.

rules.text: A roll of 2-4 on the injury chart counts as stunned.

rules.name: Impale
rules.text: A shredder sticks in the target on a 4+. The model hit and warriors in base contact with it may try to pull it out in their recovery phase on a 4+, and each attempt causes a Strength 1 hit on the model. While the shredder is stuck the model takes an automatic Strength 2 hit at the beginning of each recovery phase.

stubs.name: Splinters
stubs.note: Clockwork weapons only; one battle's worth.

rules.name: Slivers
rules.text: Every hit is at -1 Strength.

rules.name: Shard plume
rules.text: The firer is at +1 to hit and ignores cover modifiers. A successful shot hits the target and every warrior in base contact with him.

rules.name: Jamming
rules.text: A roll of 1 to hit jams the weapon, which may not be fired again until the model spends a whole turn cleaning its barrel.

flags.what: The skill table's ticks are glyphs the text layer drops: the table was read from p4's image. Master of Clocks: Combat, Shooting, Academic, Special. Dwarf engineer: Combat, Shooting, Strength, and no Special. Metallurgist and Apprentice: Academic, Speed, Special.

The seven construct rules (Need Orders, Immune to Psychology, No Pain, May Not Run, Immune to Poison, Brainless, In-built equipment) are printed once as a block. They are carried as each construct's own rules, so the four that are shared specials of ours link them, and the slot counts each fighter's entry prints sit in his In-built equipment.

The Clockwork pistol (25 gc) and Clockwork rifle (40 gc) have no rules in this PDF, and were read as our Pistol and our Handgun under the Clockworkers' names (William, 11 Nov 2026: "these are just nicknames"). The Sealed City's own Lost and Found (https://www.broheim.net/downloads/campaigns/sealedcity/Lost%20And%20Found.pdf, 1-5, text layer; read 12 Nov 2026) gives each its own entry - Clockwork pistol 8", Strength as user, Reload and Salvo; Clockwork rifle 18", Strength as user, Reload and Salvo - and its price chart sells the Clockwork pistol (25 gc Rare 8) beside the Pistol (15 gc Rare 9) and the Clockwork rifle (40 gc Rare 9) beside the Handgun (35 gc Rare 9), as four separate lines. They are different weapons, so each is now its own item at the chart's price and rarity, the two lists sell them under their own names and the Pistol and Handgun price rows they carried are gone. See the decisions.
The Heroes list prints Hammer and Staff at 3 gc each, both our Club, Mace or Hammer: carried as one line "Hammer/Staff". The Constructs list's Hammer and Mace, 3 gc each, are one line the same way.
The Constructs list is printed as 1-Slot and 2-Slot sections; our lists have no sections, so the slots are said in the list's caveat and in the In-built equipment rule.

The six Laws of Construction are carried as a new spell lore, Laws of Construction, with each law's difficulty, so the Master of Clocks can pick one. The PDF says a Law is not a spell: that is said in the warband rule of the same name.

Experimental enhancements rolls on the Stygian Mutation chart, which the setting's own Stygian Mutations PDF (https://www.broheim.net/downloads/campaigns/sealedcity/Stygian%20Mutations.pdf, 1-7, text layer; read 12 Nov 2026) prints. Its thirty D66 results are now specials: the ones that match ours link ours, the fourteen that differ or are new are the Sealed City's own mutations. The chart itself is not a table of ours. See the decisions.

Moonstones are spent by Gift of Sentience and Moonstone refinery. Lost and Found (read 12 Nov 2026) prices neither moonstones nor orichalcum tokens and is the only Sealed City document read, so the Orichalcum token stub still carries no rules and no moonstone item is made. See the decisions.
A Clockwork expedition needs at least 3 models: our templates hold no minimum, so it is not imported.
Page 7 is a scan with no text layer: it holds a picture and its caption only (opened as an image).

Lost and Found p1-3 brings the setting ten items we lacked - Krakensilver Weapon, Clockwork Lenses, Clockwork Prosthesis, Quarter Map, Lurking Fear, Moonshine, Stardust, Gaveleers, Shredders and Splinters - plus the Beast of Burden, a clockwork mount in the bestiary with the page's profile. Each is declared here for the setting's five warband types, since the price chart is the setting's shop and no warband list sells most of them. The Krakensilver Weapon is "4 x Price" on the chart, so its row carries no figure.

Lost and Found p4-5 is the setting's price chart, read in place of the rulebook's. Every line but seven matches our own price and rarity, so only those seven take a row for the setting's types: Pike 12 gc Rare 9, Blunderbuss 30 gc Rare 10, Handgun 35 gc Rare 9, Hunting Rifle 200 gc Rare 12, Pistol 15 gc Rare 9, Barding 30 gc Rare 8 (ours is 80 gc) and Superior Blackpowder 30 gc Rare 12. The chart's Plate armour is 70 gc Rare 9 where the House Guard's own entry, already imported as the setting's item, is 70 gc Rare 7: ours is unchanged. Its River Boat is our Rowboat and its Superior Black powder our Superior Blackpowder. See the decisions.
